exact_statement.text: Let N >= 2, d=4, G=SU(N), and 0 < beta < 1/48. Let mu_L be the SZZ L-periodic pure Wilson measures, periodically embedded in the common product configuration space, and let mu be their whole-sequence weak limit. For the site reflection r(n0,nsp)=(-n0,nsp), with its induced oriented-link involution theta, every bounded continuous gauge-invariant cylinder F whose link support lies strictly in n0>0 satisfies integral conjugate(F(theta Q)) F(Q) dmu(Q) >= 0.

assumptions: N is an integer at least 2
the theory is the fermion-free SU(N) Wilson plaquette theory
beta is positive and satisfies the SZZ strong-coupling bound beta < 1/[16(d-1)] = 1/48
finite volumes use the isotropic odd periods ell_j=2m_j+1, a cofinal subsequence of the SZZ sequence
positive-time cylinders are supported on finitely many oriented links strictly in n0>0
theta is induced from the site reflection on oriented paths, so a reflected temporal positive link is represented by the inverse matrix on the corresponding positive orientation

anchors: equations (1.1)-(1.3): periodic Wilson measure and SU(N) range
Theorem 1.2(2): every tight limit is the same and the whole finite-volume sequence converges weakly
paragraph before equation (1.5): periodic embedding into the common compact product space
equation (2): Wilson plaquette coefficient 1/(2 g0^2) over both plaquette orientations
equation (4): OS positivity for gauge-invariant positive-time polynomials
equations (20)-(23) and Proposition 1: positivity of the pure gauge transfer kernel for SU(N)
boundary paragraph and equation (28): periodic gauge boundary conditions in space and time on odd site counts
Proposition 2: reconstruction and the stated implication to OS positivity

derivation_audit.reason: Luescher sums the two orientations with coefficient 1/(2 g0^2), hence each unoriented plaquette contributes g0^-2 Re Tr(U_p). Setting g0^-2=N beta matches SZZ. The relevant positivity is the separately displayed pure gauge kernel; no fermionic determinant or gauge-fixed measure is transported.

Set Luescher's spatial and temporal half-widths equal to m_j. The resulting period 2m_j+1 matches the isotropic SZZ odd subsequence. The site reflection is well defined on each odd torus and its induced action on oriented links agrees with the infinite-lattice action on any fixed source and reflected source once j is large enough.

Luescher equation (4), the positive pure gauge kernel, and Proposition 2 give the nonnegative quadratic form for gauge-invariant positive-time polynomial cylinders on the matching finite periodic pure Wilson measure.

For a polynomial cylinder P, conjugate(P(theta Q))P(Q) is a bounded continuous cylinder on the common compact product space. Whole-sequence weak convergence therefore transports its finite-volume nonnegativity along the odd cofinal subsequence to mu.

Matrix coefficients and their conjugates form a unital self-adjoint point-separating algebra on each finite SU(N)^m. Stone-Weierstrass gives uniform approximation. Haar averaging over the compact gauge group at the finitely many incident vertices preserves polynomiality and link support, contracts the uniform error, and produces gauge-invariant approximants. The OS quadratic functional is uniform-norm continuous.

transfer_interfaces.source_A_to_source_B: same fermion-free Wilson density after g0^-2=N beta, same odd periodic torus, same induced site reflection, same gauge-invariant polynomial positive-time algebra
transfer_interfaces.finite_to_infinite: SZZ periodic embedding into one compact product space plus whole-sequence weak convergence; only bounded continuous reflected cylinders are transported
transfer_interfaces.polynomial_to_continuous: uniform Stone-Weierstrass approximation followed by finite-vertex compact gauge averaging
forbidden_transfers: SZZ support-distance clustering to OS transfer moments
finite-cutoff reflection positivity to a continuum theory
reflection positivity alone to a nonzero physical Hamiltonian gap

falsifiers.test: compare oriented/unoriented plaquette sums and require g0^-2=N beta
use only the fermion-free Wilson measure and the separately positive pure gauge kernel
identify odd periods, site reflection, temporal-link inversion, and eventual seam avoidance
require the reflected quadratic integrand to be a bounded continuous finite cylinder
uniform matrix-coordinate approximation followed by contractive compact gauge averaging

proposal_only_rakl_lesson.text: For a theorem-like application step, make the complete current-gate packet, including obstruction-transformation review and public pre-candidate trace, a public parent of the first result-capable commit. A prospective issue contract does not substitute for those content-bound artifacts, and later files cannot backfill chronology.
proposal_only_rakl_lesson.validation_obligation: On a fresh child atom, require the gate receipt commit to be an ancestor of the candidate commit and make tests fail if any required current-framework event or content-bound artifact is absent.
